Have you ever been sitting in the room when someone is on the phone, and all you hear is a one sided conversation? Sometimes what they say might seem interesting, and you wonder what the other person said to elicit that response? Isn't it slightly annoying?

Same thing is true in social forums such as this one. There's a thread of discussion, and all of a sudden you see [deleted], then an answer, then [deleted] and an answer....then [deleted]. A back and forth of which you only see/hear/read one side.

I propose that [deleted] comments do not actually get deleted, but rather just the username is removed (after all, people should still be able to disassociate themselves with a comment they made) but for the sake of preserving context, leave the comment itself.

Maybe append some kind of message at the beginning like: The following comment was removed by the author on [date]. It has been archived for context. and then either show the comment as quoted text, or set it that the comment is collapsed, but can be expanded to be viewed.

What do you fine voaters think?
Er, no. People often delete their comments because they contain personal information.
Then how about we give users choices to completely remove the comment vs just removing their username when they click on delete?
Bad idea, in my opinion. If someone posts personal information they should be able to remove it, if they decide it wasn't prudent to do so.

I hadn't thought about that...though people shouldn't be putting personal information up in public forums such as this, I can understand that things happen and mistakes can be made.

Would it be feasible to send delete requests to a mod queue or would that be too overwhelming?

Ex. Hit delete and enter a reason. If for personal info, mods can redact or remove as needed. If any other reason, just username is removed.

Like I said, seeing a bunch of deleted comments in a string of discussion kind of throws off the whole thing, seeing just a one sided conversation. Though now I don't have an idea how to remedy this given the possiblity of deleting personal info.
